title: Orchestrate shadow + canary pipeline for FP8 profile rollouts on Hopper (E4M3/E5M2)
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: Deliver an automated orchestration that performs shadow validation and staged canary rollouts for FP8 quantization profiles (E4M3/E5M2 selectors) on Hopper GPUs, reducing regression risk and improving activation stability. Background: Recent manual rollouts uncovered two classes of failures: ephemeral model instability tied to per-layer dynamic range shifts, and latency/throughput regressions under realistic traffic patterns. We need a repeatable pipeline that validates candidate quant profiles against production-like workloads, enforces telemetry-based gates, automates fallback, and provides clear runbooks for on-call escalation.
acceptance_criteria: Shadow validation job runs daily and on every candidate profile build; produces pass/fail with aggregated accuracy metrics and per-batch divergence histograms.
Canary orchestration can progressively enable a profile for 0->1->5->25->100% traffic segments with automated rollback on gating conditions.
E4M3/E5M2 selector decision is recorded and logged per-request; mismatches between selector and observed numeric stability trigger an annotation for retraining/calibration.
End-to-end runbook exists and is tested in a dry-run canary; on-call can trigger emergency rollback within 2 minutes using the console action.
No customer-facing accuracy regressions beyond the agreed nyquist thresholds for any monitored prompt set in the synthetic validation suite.
implementation_notes: Reuse existing calibration runner (calib-service) but add a 'shadow' mode to run candidate FP8 kernels side-by-side with baseline INT8/FP16 on a sampled request stream.
Introduce a canary-scheduler component that uses traffic buckets keyed by customer tier + region; respects reserved capacity for Dedicated clusters.
Implement a lightweight comparator that computes per-request token-level perplexity delta, top-k token divergence, and model output hashing for fast equality checks.
Persist selector decisions (E4M3 vs E5M2) and calibration stats to the quant-profile metadata store for audit and rollback analysis.
Add telemetry tags to traces for 'quant_profile_id' and 'shadow_result' to surface side-by-side latency and error budget impact in the Console.
test_plan: Create a synthetic validation set (1k prompts across retrieval, multi-turn chat, and summarization) with known golden outputs for regression checks.
Run continuous shadow validation on a subset of production traffic (1% sample) for 48 hours and verify statistical stability of quality metrics.
Chaos test: inject transient GPU OOM and kernel fallback to verify automatic selector downgrade and no data loss.
Performance test: measure p95/p99 latency and tokens/sec under realistic batching distribution; compare against baseline and ensure latency SLO degradation < 5%.
Canary dry-run: perform 0->1->5% traffic step-up in a staging cluster and validate both automated and manual rollback flows.
rollout_plan: Step 0: Merge canary orchestration code and calibration improvements behind feature flag 'fp8-orchestrator'.
Step 1: Run daily shadow validation for 7 days on candidate profiles; require zero critical regressions to proceed.
Step 2: Dry-run canary in staging with real traffic replay for one customer segment.
Step 3: Gradual production ramp: 0% -> 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with 2-hour observation windows and automated gate evaluation at each step.
Step 4: Full enablement and archive previous profile as fallback; emit release note with quant-profile ID and observed telemetry summary.
monitoring_and_gates: Quality gate: rolling 1k-sample KL divergence < 0.012 and top-1 token match rate > 98% compared to baseline (or explanatory note if specialized workload).
Latency gate: p95 latency increase < 5% and p99 < 10% relative to baseline at same batching level.
Error budget gate: < 0.1% increase in model error responses (invalid tokens, decode failures) over a 1-hour window.
Resource gate: GPU memory overhead per replica < 3% and no sustained increase in scheduling preemption events.
Alerting: Pager on 'canary_quant_profile_violation' when any gate breaches for >15 minutes, and auto-rollback when breach persists for >30 minutes.
Telemetry payloads: include sample_id, prompt_hash, quant_profile_id, selector_choice, shadow_metrics (kl, topk_match, latency_diff).
